how: deck_images.py extracts every embedded image (pdfimages -png, soft masks kept for cutouts) and a 2x render of every page (pdftoppm -r 144, 2880x1620) into deck/ (gitignored: the repo is public, nothing from the PDF is committed), then resolves each entry below to deck/resolved/<id>.png. source 'embedded' takes the largest picture on that slide (or 'pick': its index on the slide, 0 = first, as listed in deck/contact.html); source 'page' takes the whole slide render. 'crop': [left, top, width, height] as fractions of the source; 'tiles': several such crops laid out in a grid of 'cols' columns (a wide row made to fit a tall slot); 'matte': the colour a cutout (an image with a soft mask) is laid on, the colour of the slot it stands in. 'fit': 'cover' fills the slot when the source is big enough, else the deck shows it as a print at a size that stays sharp; 'contain' always shows the whole image; 'cutout' stands it on the slot's bottom edge; 'zoom' below 1 shows a print smaller (a headline taken from the deck). 'consent': 'verify' = shows a person other than Josh, a client, a name or a private conversation: the owner confirms, then set 'confirmed': true (the voiced build refuses unconfirmed ones, and the presented deck shows a labelled slot instead). 'used_on' lists the webinar slides ([SLIDE: ...] titles in script-ai.md) that show it. 'retired' lists ids from the March 2026 deck that this deck has no source for. 'masks': solid boxes [left, top, width, height] (fractions of the image after crop or tiles, optional fill colour as a fifth item; default the background colour around the box) over lines that must not be shown, such as crude wording in a client's chat; every masked image is checked by eye after --resolve.
